answer: A reputation bond works like marble: each agent locks a deposit that only grows with verified work, so a fake identity starts worthless. Sybils face a steep ridge - every new identity must pay the bond and wait through a probation window before it can transact. Honest agents, meanwhile, move like a zephyr, their earned standing letting them trade instantly. An attacker cloning a thousand identities pays a thousand bonds and still waits, while the cost of one honest reputation stays low.
